cards.body: Thirteen hairpins on Europe’s oldest road pass, car-free climbing to 1,370 m above Tržič.

cards.title: Kamničanka

cards.title: Mali vrh
cards.body: Forest road to a quiet lookout above Jezersko, Grintovec, Košuta and Storžič in one calm half-day.

intro.body: We’re Jakob and Tanja, the small team behind Zyflow in Slovenia. We’re building Zyflow so every ride comes with good places to stop, a charger when you need one, and a welcome for your bike. Questions or ideas? We read every message.

testimonial.body: Riders choose where to stop in Zyflow before they leave. Put your café, restaurant or stay in front of them, with your bike parking, storage or charger on the map.

items.title: places other maps miss
items.body: Most maps show you roads. Zyflow shows you where to stop: stays, coffee and restaurants that welcome bikes, with parking, storage and charging marked.

items.title: safety you can see
items.body: Road closures, roadworks and events on your route, bike theft by area, and chargers placed where your battery needs them.

items.title: a battery plan you can trust
items.body: Zyflow plans around your range, the climbs, wind and temperature, so the ride does not end early.

appStage.body: Battery, elevation, chargers, and weather in one plan, so you leave knowing the ride will finish.

steps.title: explore
steps.body: Open the map and find stays, coffee stops and restaurants that welcome bikes, plus chargers, water and repair as you zoom in.

steps.title: plan
steps.body: Connect the places into a ride. Zyflow plans your battery around the climbs and places chargers before you need them.

steps.title: ride
steps.body: Check road closures before you leave and see where bikes get stolen. Then ride, and stop wherever looks good.

items.title: find bike-friendly places
items.body: Bike parking, secure storage, a pump or a charger, marked on every place. Filter the map to show only places that welcome bikes.

items.title: ride feeling safe
items.body: See road closures and roadworks before you leave, check bike theft by area, and plan your battery with chargers along the way.

items.title: growing across Europe
items.body: Live in 8 countries, starting from Slovenia, Croatia and Austria, and growing country by country.

faq.title: common questions
faq.footnote: Questions, feedback or a place we’re missing? Email support@zyflow.eu. We read every message.

items.a: Zyflow is a free app for finding bike-friendly places: stays, coffee stops, restaurants, chargers and bike services. You can see road closures and bike theft by area, and plan a ride between the places with your battery in mind.
Yes. Zyflow is free to download and use on iOS and Android.
Any bike: road, gravel, touring, mountain and e-bikes. With an e-bike, you also get the battery plan and chargers along the way.

items.q: How do I know a place is bike-friendly?
items.a: Places with bike parking, secure storage, a pump or a charger are marked, and you can filter the map to show only bike-friendly places.

items.q: I run a café, hotel or bike shop. Can I be on Zyflow?
items.a: Yes. Get in touch through the contact form and we’ll add your place, with your bike parking, storage or charger on the map.

hero.lede: Twenty rides from Kranj, Tržič and Jezersko, lake loops, alpine passes and quiet gravel. Pick a route, then open it in Zyflow.

cards.title: Blejčanka
cards.body: A full-day loop from Kranj to Lake Bled, Radovljica’s old square, Kropa’s forge streets, then the lake shore before the climb home.

cards.title: Jezerjanka
cards.body: Follow the Kokra past Preddvor into Slovenia’s first Mountain Village, glacier valleys, alpine farms and quieter roads than the lake circuits.

cards.title: Jezerski vrh
cards.body: Climb to the former border crossing, then continue to Ankova planina for a full panorama of Ravenska Kočna and the Kamnik Alps.

cards.title: Planine pod Košuto
cards.body: Tržič’s alpine flagship: forest roads and pasture shelves under the long white wall of Košuta, big climbing, bigger views.

cards.title: Tržič – Jezersko
cards.body: A linking ride between two alpine valleys, from Tržič’s Karawanks flank across to the glacier bowl of Jezersko.

cards.title: Dom pod Storžičem
cards.body: A hut-day climb toward Storžič, forest gradients, mountain air and a clear turnaround at Dom pod Storžičem.

cards.title: Prelaz Ljubelj
cards.body: Thirteen hairpins on Europe’s oldest road pass, closed to cars, open to bikes, with a hut at 1,370 m.

cards.title: Rožnovenska pot
cards.body: A culture-forward loop from Tržič through Brezje pri Tržiču, churches, valley towns and riding that stays scenic without going fully alpine.

cards.title: Dobrča
cards.body: A full alpine day toward Dobrča, long climbs, ridge air and the feeling of riding the Karawanks rather than around them.

cards.title: Udin boršt
cards.body: Foothill gravel around Udin boršt, forest tracks, gentle rollers and enough variety to feel adventurous without a high pass.

cards.title: Pot treh zvonov
cards.body: The easy family loop of the Tržič set, gentle terrain, village bells and a rhythm that works for mixed abilities.

cards.title: Kriva jelka
cards.body: Into the Udin boršt nature reserve toward the crooked fir, shaded tracks and a landmark finish in the forest.

cards.title: Gozd – Udin boršt
cards.body: A varied foothill loop linking Gozd with Udin boršt, more climbing than the family routes, still short of alpine grades.

cards.title: Kamničanka
cards.body: Flat-leaning loop via Šenčur, Adergas, Cerklje and Kamnik, Arboretum Volčji Potok, Strmol Castle and Slovenia’s only motorway bike bridge.

cards.title: Ljubljančanka
cards.body: South from Kranj to the capital, Smlednik Castle, Tivoli and Ljubljana Castle on a day that mixes countryside with city arrival.

cards.title: Ločanka
cards.body: Into Škofja Loka’s medieval core, Capuchin bridges, the castle hill and Crngrob church on one of the flower’s prettiest days.

cards.title: Mali vrh
cards.body: Quiet forest road to the Mali vrh lookout, Virnikov Grintovec, Košuta and Storžič in one calm Jezersko half-day.

cards.title: Ravenska Kočna
cards.body: Past Planšarsko jezero into Ravenska Kočna and up to Štularjeva planina, cirque walls and a cargo cableway below Češka koča.

cards.title: Spodnji Virnik
cards.body: Short educational loop to the tufa quarry and Spodnji Virnik farm, watch rock forming at the spring, then taste dairy on the meadow.

cards.title: Tržičanka
cards.body: North to Tržič’s old town and the Karawanks gateway, Kamen Castle ruins, valley roads and a taste of the alpine network beyond.

hero.lede: 134 km from Ljubljana to the Adriatic, past bike-friendly stays, coffee stops and restaurants, with chargers and bike services along the way.

body.intro: Ljubljana to Trieste crosses three landscapes in a day: the green edge of the capital, the stone villages of the Karst and the Adriatic coast. Zyflow lines up the bike-friendly places in between, so the ride is as much about where you stop as how far you go.

sections.title: Leaving Ljubljana
sections.body: Roll out past Vrhnika on quiet roads. The first coffee stop comes early, and it is worth it: the climb onto the plateau starts soon after. Zyflow shows your expected battery along the whole route, so you can pace the start instead of guessing.

sections.title: Karst villages & stops
sections.body: Between Postojna and Divača the road rises and falls through stone villages, with family restaurants and guesthouses that welcome bikes. Charging and water sit right where the hardest sections begin.
bullets: See road closures and roadworks on the route before you leave
Know which places have bike parking, secure storage or a charger

sections.title: Descent to the Adriatic
sections.body: After Sežana the plateau ends and the road drops toward the Gulf of Trieste. Finish with a coffee by the sea, or stay the night and ride back tomorrow.

hero.storyTitle: Great places to stop are everywhere. Most maps just don’t show them.
hero.storyBody: We’re Jakob and Tanja, the team behind Zyflow, made by HERKO d.o.o. in Slovenia. Zyflow helps cyclists and e-bike riders find bike-friendly stays, coffee stops, restaurants and chargers, and ride between them feeling safe. Today it is live on iOS and Android in 8 countries, with 7,400+ chargers mapped and data from partners like Open Data Hub. Next: more countries, more places, and more ways to keep riders safe.

items.body: Zyflow is here so you can say yes to the detour. Every place shows whether your bike is welcome, so the next stop is a choice, not a gamble.
Road closures, bike theft by area and chargers along the way. We show what we know, so you can decide before you ride.
We only promise what the app does today. When something is still being built, we say so, and we listen when riders tell us what to fix next.
Zyflow is free on iOS and Android, for every rider and every bike. Start with one stop, then go further.

e-bike-charging-at-hospitality-stops.title: why e-bike charging at hospitality stops matters
e-bike-charging-at-hospitality-stops.lede: A charger at a café or guesthouse can decide how far a ride goes. Here's why, and how to find one.

body.p1: There's a particular kind of calm you only get when you know where the next charger is. You stop checking the battery every five minutes. You take the detour to the viewpoint. You order the second coffee. When a stop isn't visible online, that calm disappears, and longer rides shrink to whatever feels safe to guess.
body.p2: Plenty of cafés, restaurants and guesthouses already let riders plug in an e-bike. Very few of them say so anywhere a rider would look. The socket is there, the owner is happy to help, but for anyone planning a ride it might as well not exist.
body.p3: That's the gap Zyflow is built to close. In the app, charging sits in the Utility layer on the Explore map, next to water, bike shops, repair and bike parking. Turn it on and you see where you can top up before you leave home, not after the battery warning starts blinking.
body.h2: a charger changes the shape of the day
body.p4: A known charging stop does more than add range. It turns a ride into a plan. Lunch becomes the moment the battery fills back up. A guesthouse with a socket becomes the reason a two-day loop works. The places worth stopping at and the places that keep you rolling are often the same places.
body.li1: Find it before you go. Open Explore, switch on Utility and look at the stretch where your battery will be lowest
body.li2: Pair it with a stop you'd enjoy anyway. A charger at a café beats a charger in a car park
body.li3: Have a plan B. Note a second option nearby, in case the first one is closed or busy
body.h3: plan for the climb, not the café
body.p5: Battery drain is not even. A flat valley road costs little, while a long climb, a headwind or a cold morning can cost a lot. When you plan a route in Zyflow, the battery plan takes the climbs and the weather into account and shows the chargers along the way, so you know where the tight sections are before you reach them.
body.quote: "If a charger isn't visible online, many riders never find it. And longer rides shrink to whatever feels safe to guess."
body.h4: if you run a place with a spare socket
body.p6: Riders are looking for you. Listing a café, restaurant, guesthouse or charger on Zyflow is free while we launch, and you can manage your own details, photos and opening hours through the partner portal. A socket and a friendly "yes, of course" is often all it takes to become the stop a ride is planned around.

planning-your-first-battery-aware-day-ri.title: planning your first battery-aware day ride
planning-your-first-battery-aware-day-ri.lede: Range, climbs and chargers: a simple way to plan a day ride you'll actually finish.

body.p1: The best first long ride on an e-bike isn't the most ambitious one. It's the one where you come home with battery to spare, a few good stops behind you and the feeling that next time you could go further. Here's a simple way to plan it.
body.p2: The number on the box is a best case. Real range depends on the assist level you actually use, your weight and luggage, the tyres and the weather. Set your range in Zyflow the way you really ride, not the way the brochure rides. If you're not sure, be a little conservative. Finishing with 20% left feels a lot better than finishing with 2%.
body.p3: A rolling countryside day is where almost every rider should begin. The rhythm is predictable, the climbs are short and you get a feel for how your battery behaves without the mountains making the decisions for you. Browse the routes by region and ride type, and choose one that matches the day you want, not the day you think you should manage.
body.h3: read the battery plan before you leave
body.p4: When you plan a ride, Zyflow builds a battery plan from the route's elevation, your range settings and the wind and weather forecast. It shows where the effort will be and where the chargers sit along the way.
body.li1: Look for the tight section. The part of the ride with the hardest climb and the furthest charger is the one to plan around
body.li2: Check the wind. A headwind on the way home can cost more than the climb on the way out
body.li3: Mark a charging stop. Even if you don't need it, knowing it's there changes how you ride
body.quote: "Finishing with 20% left feels a lot better than finishing with 2%."
body.h4: plan the stops, not just the line
body.p5: A good day ride is more than distance. Turn on Coffee and Restaurants in Explore and pick a place to stop around the halfway point. If it has a charger or bike parking, even better. Stops are where the ride becomes a day out, and they're easy to plan once you can see them.
body.p6: After a ride or two you'll know how your bike behaves on climbs, in the cold and with a full bag. That's when longer days and bigger mountains start to make sense. Build up slowly, keep a charger in the plan, and let each ride teach you something for the next one.

what-makes-a-place-bike-friendly.title: what makes a place bike-friendly?
what-makes-a-place-bike-friendly.lede: Bike parking, secure storage, a pump, a charger. What we look for, and how to filter for it in the app.

body.p1: "Bike-friendly" gets used a lot. A sticker on a door, a line on a booking site, a rack that fits two bikes on a good day. For riders, it should mean something more useful: you can arrive by bike, leave it somewhere you trust, and enjoy the place without worrying about what's happening outside.
body.p2: In Zyflow, a place counts as bike-friendly when it offers real facilities for riders, not just goodwill. The ones that matter most:
body.li1: Bike parking. Somewhere proper to lock up, close to the entrance
body.li2: Secure storage. A locked room, garage or shed, especially important for stays and expensive e-bikes
body.li3: A pump and basic tools. Small things that save a ride
body.li4: Charging. A socket for an e-bike, ideally somewhere you can sit and wait
body.p3: We combine open map data, regional tourism data from partners like Open Data Hub, and details that businesses add themselves. When a hotel, café or restaurant manages its own listing, the information tends to be more accurate and more current. That's why we're making it free for places to list and update themselves while we launch.
body.quote: "You can arrive by bike, leave it somewhere you trust, and enjoy the place without worrying about what's happening outside."
body.h3: how to find these places in the app
body.p4: Open Explore and switch on the layers you care about: Stay, Coffee or Restaurants. Then turn on Bike-friendly only. The map now shows just the places with real facilities for riders, so you can plan a lunch stop or a night's stay knowing the bike is taken care of too.
body.p5: For peace of mind, you can also turn on the Safety layer to see bike theft by area. It's a simple way to decide where secure storage really matters.
body.p6: If you have a rack, a storage room or a spare socket, riders want to know. Request access to the partner portal, add your facilities and photos, and your place shows up for riders who filter for exactly that.

zyflow-is-live-on-ios-and-android.title: zyflow is live on ios and android
zyflow-is-live-on-ios-and-android.lede: Free on both stores and live in 8 countries. Here's what to try on your next ride.

body.p1: Zyflow is now free on the App Store and Google Play, and live in 8 countries. We're just getting started, and we built it around one simple idea: explore bike-friendly places, and ride there feeling safe. Here's what to try first.
body.p2: Open Explore and you'll see the map in layers. Stay, Coffee and Restaurants show you where to stop, sleep and eat. Utility brings in the practical things: charging, water, bike shops, repair and bike parking. Turn on only what you need, and the map stays clean.
body.p3: Switch on Bike-friendly only and the map narrows to places with real facilities for riders, like bike parking, secure storage, a pump or a charger. It's the quickest way to find a café you can actually ride to and a stay that has room for your bike.
body.p4: Before you head out, check Road conditions nearby on Home. Zyflow shows closures, construction and events around you and along a planned route, so you're not surprised halfway through. The Safety layer on the map shows bike theft by area, which helps when you're deciding where to leave the bike.
body.quote: "Explore bike-friendly places. Ride there feeling safe."
body.h4: plan a ride when you want one
body.p5: Found a place you want to reach? Plan a route there. On an e-bike, the battery plan takes the climbs, your range and the weather into account and shows chargers along the way. Planning works offline-ready too, so a patchy signal in the hills doesn't leave you guessing.
body.p6: This is the first version, and the map gets better with every place added. If you run a café, restaurant, stay or charger, listing it is free while we launch. If you spot something missing or wrong, tell us. We read everything.

reading-elevation-before-a-cross-border-.title: reading elevation before a cross-border ride
reading-elevation-before-a-cross-border-.lede: How to read the climbs on a ride like Ljubljana to Trieste, and where to plan your stops.

body.p1: A ride from Ljubljana to Trieste sounds like it should be downhill all the way. You start inland and finish at the sea. But the Karst plateau sits in between, and the shape of the climb before the coast decides how the whole day feels. Reading the elevation before you leave is what turns a hard day into a good one.
body.h1: look at the shape, not just the total
body.p2: Total climbing tells you how hard a ride is. The elevation profile tells you when it's hard. A long steady rise in the first half feels very different from a steep ramp late in the day, even if the numbers are the same. In Zyflow, the elevation profile is colour-coded by gradient and the main climbs are marked, so you can see at a glance where the work is.
body.li1: The steady rise. On a route like this, most of the effort comes as you climb gradually onto the Karst. It's rarely steep, but it's long, and it's where the battery works hardest
body.li2: The high ground. Once you're up, the plateau rolls. This is the place to stop, eat and recharge before the coast
body.li3: The drop to the sea. The descent towards Trieste is the reward. Take it easy, the roads get busier near the city
body.quote: "Total climbing tells you how hard a ride is. The elevation profile tells you when it's hard."
body.h3: plan your stops around the climbs
body.p3: The best place for a break is usually just before or just after the biggest effort. Turn on Coffee, Restaurants and Utility in Explore and look at what sits along the route near the top of the climb. A lunch stop with a charger there means you start the descent with a full battery and a full stomach.
body.p4: Zyflow is live in 8 countries, so places and routes don't stop at the border. Before you go, check Road conditions along your planned route for closures or construction on either side, and remember that opening hours and holidays can differ from one country to the next.
body.h5: ride it once, read it better next time
body.p5: After your first cross-border ride, the elevation profile will start to look different. You'll know what a long rise feels like on your bike, and you'll plan the next one faster. Start with a route like Ljubljana to Trieste, plan the stops around the climb, and enjoy the sea at the end.

blejcanka.lede: Kranj’s western petal to Lake Bled: nearly 80 km, close to 1,000 m of climbing, and the classic Gorenjska postcard, Kropa, the lake, and Radovljica’s square.
blejcanka.intro: Blejčanka is the beauty day of the Kranjska roža. You leave the Sava plain, climb toward Jamnik until the Karawanks open, drop into Kropa’s ironworking streets, then arrive at Bled’s castle rock and shoreline before swinging through Radovljica on the way home. It is long enough to matter and scenic enough to justify every metre.
blejcanka.metaDescription: Blejčanka, Kranj to Lake Bled past Kropa and Radovljica: 79 km and 944 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Climb toward the Karawanks
sections.body: From central Kranj the road tilts up toward Jamnik. After a few kilometres of honest climbing the ridge views appear, a clear signal you have left the flat petal routes behind.
sections.body2: Kropa follows: narrow lanes, forge heritage, and one of the most atmospheric villages on any of the flower rides. Pause here before the landscape opens fully toward the lake.

sections.title: Bled, then Radovljica
sections.body: Bled is the emotional peak of the day, island church, castle, and the shoreline loop that every visitor recognises. Ride it with traffic awareness; the reward is the postcard you came for.
sections.body2: Radovljica’s baroque square is the cultural cool-down before the return toward Kranj. By then the climbing is largely behind you, but the legs will feel the full 944 m.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: This is an e-bike sweet spot: almost 80 km and nearly a vertical kilometre. Pin chargers near Bled and a lunch stop in Kropa or Radovljica before you roll out.
sections.body2: Check wind on the exposed sections and save an early café in Kranj for the finish. Open the route in Zyflow when you want navigation plus bike-friendly places on the same map.

jezerjanka.lede: North from Kranj along the Kokra into Slovenia’s first Mountain Village, glacier valleys, alpine farms and a quieter rhythm than the lake circuits.
jezerjanka.intro: Jezerjanka is the alpine petal of the Kranjska roža. Instead of postcard lakes you get working high farms, sudden rock walls and the wide green bowl of Jezersko under the Kamnik–Savinja Alps. At 76 km with around 600 m of climbing it is committing without becoming a race.
jezerjanka.metaDescription: Jezerjanka follows the Kokra from Kranj to Jezersko: 76 km and 603 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Up the Kokra
sections.body: Leave Kranj and settle into the valley road through Preddvor. The Kokra narrows gradually; traffic thins; the peaks start to stack ahead of you.
sections.body2: This is where the day changes character, from town touring into mountain valley riding. Keep snacks handy; services grow thinner the higher you go.

sections.title: Into Jezersko
sections.body: Jezersko opens as a glacial amphitheatre: meadows, farmhouses and ridges that earned the village its Mountain Village status. Ride the valley floor, then decide whether to add a short local loop if legs allow.
sections.body2: The return follows the same corridor south. Descend with room for hikers and farm traffic, and save a café stop in Preddvor if you skipped lunch higher up.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Map water and food before you leave Kranj, the middle stretch is lean. A charger near the valley mouth is insurance on an e-bike day.
sections.body2: Pair Jezerjanka with a quieter Jezersko half-day (Mali vrh or Ravenska Kočna) if you overnight. Open the main line in Zyflow for navigation and place filters.

jezerski-vrh.lede: Climb to the former border crossing, then on to Ankova planina for a full panorama of Ravenska Kočna and the Kamnik Alps.
jezerski-vrh.intro: Jezerski vrh is the classic Jezersko panorama ride: mineral spring at the start, border saddle in the middle, meadow lookout at the end. About 18.2 km and 457 m fit in roughly two and a half hours.
jezerski-vrh.metaDescription: Jezerski vrh to Ankova planina, a panorama above Ravenska Kočna: 18.2 km and 457 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: From slatina to the saddle
sections.body: Share the early road with road cyclists aiming for the border. Fill a little Jezerska slatina at the organised point, a sip is enough; save more for the return bag.
sections.body2: Climb to the former border crossing. Between the Slovenian and Austrian buildings, turn left for the steeper finish.

sections.title: Ankova planina
sections.body: Views open fast: Ravenska Kočna, the Kamnik–Savinja wall, then the whole Jezersko valley with Veliki vrh, Kozji vrh and Storžič. Continue on easier road to Ankova planina and the old military post.
sections.body2: Return the same way. Detour to St Andrew’s church and Šenkova domačija on the way down if time allows.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Weather turns fast on the saddle, check shelter options before the last climb. Pin the slatina and a valley lunch.
sections.body2: Open Jezerski vrh in Zyflow as the bigger-view sibling to Mali vrh on a Jezersko weekend.

k11-planine-pod-kosuto.lede: Tržič’s alpine flagship: forest roads and pasture shelves under Košuta’s long white wall, big climbing, bigger views.
k11-planine-pod-kosuto.intro: K11 is the high signature of the Tržič network. You leave town for steep forest approaches that open onto a chain of planine under Košuta, with views that stretch toward Austria. This is a full mountain day, not a café loop.
k11-planine-pod-kosuto.metaDescription: Alpine ride from Tržič onto the pastures under Košuta: 1740 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Into the Karawanks foothills
sections.body: Climb out of Tržič as the asphalt thins and the forest takes over. Gradients come in waves; shade helps, but the elevation keeps coming.
sections.body2: Early turnaround options exist if weather shifts. The higher pastures reward those who keep a reserve for the last shelves.

sections.title: Pastures under Košuta
sections.body: The limestone ridge of Košuta stays in view once you clear the trees. Alpine huts and meadow tracks define the middle of the day, shared with hikers, cattle and silence.
sections.body2: Descend with discipline. Forest roads cut speed slowly; loose sections punish late braking.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Confirm hut openings and water before you commit. Pin an emergency descent and a town café for the finish.
sections.body2: Open K11 in Zyflow when you want the line on the map with weather and place context, this is not a route to improvise hungry.

k16-trzic-jezersko.lede: A linking alpine day from Tržič’s Karawanks flank across to the glacier bowl of Jezersko, valley to valley, sustained climbing.
k16-trzic-jezersko.intro: K16 is the bridge in the Tržič shortlist: fewer postcard stops, more committed mountain kilometres, and a true change of valley when you finally drop toward Jezersko.
k16-trzic-jezersko.metaDescription: A forest link from Tržič across to Jezersko: 1299 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Leaving Tržič
sections.body: Climb away from town into forest that keeps gaining. The early kilometres set the tone, this is a transfer with teeth, not a scenic meander.
sections.body2: Carry more food than you think. Services in the middle are thin compared with the lake petals out of Kranj.

sections.title: Into Jezersko
sections.body: The high traverse eventually tips you toward Jezersko’s open meadows and glacial walls. The contrast with Tržič’s industrial gateway is the point of the ride.
sections.body2: Decide in advance whether Jezersko is the finish (overnight) or a turnaround. Both work; only one should be improvised.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Plan charging and meals at both ends. Mark a bail-out if weather closes the high section.
sections.body2: Open K16 in Zyflow to keep the full corridor visible and to browse Jezersko’s shorter loops for the next morning.

k21-dom-pod-storzicem.lede: A focused hut day from Tržič toward Dom pod Storžičem, forest gradients, mountain air and a clear turnaround under Storžič’s pyramid.
k21-dom-pod-storzicem.intro: K21 is built around one goal: reach the hut under Storžič, eat, then descend with fresh attention for Tržič’s streets. It is shorter than Košuta or Ljubelj in spirit, still honestly alpine.
k21-dom-pod-storzicem.metaDescription: A shorter climb from Tržič to Dom pod Storžičem: 280 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Forest approach
sections.body: Climb from town into trees that frame glimpses of the summit. The gradient is steady rather than theatrical, good rhythm riding.
sections.body2: Shared tracks mean courtesy. Announce passes and expect hikers near the hut.

sections.title: Hut and descent
sections.body: Dom pod Storžičem is the pause that defines the day. Check opening times; a closed hut turns a celebration into a cold sandwich stop.
sections.body2: Descend the way you came. Brake early on loose corners and save a café in Tržič for the emotional finish.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin hut hours and a downhill coffee before you leave. Weather under Storžič can shift while you climb.
sections.body2: Open K21 in Zyflow for the approach line and to keep the hut location obvious when the forest closes in.

k35-prelaz-ljubelj.lede: Tržič’s signature pass: thirteen hairpins on Europe’s oldest road pass, mostly car-free, with a hut at 1,370 m and about 900 m of climbing.
k35-prelaz-ljubelj.intro: K35 is the ride people mean when they say “Ljubelj by bike.” From the bus station in Tržič you climb through Podljubelj, share a careful stretch of main road, then take the historic pass that is closed to cars most of the year. The last 300 vertical metres are steep; the hut and the view into Austria are the payoff.
k35-prelaz-ljubelj.metaTitle: K35 Prelaz Ljubelj (26 km, 900 m) | Zyflow
k35-prelaz-ljubelj.metaDescription: Climb the old Ljubelj pass from Tržič, closed to cars: 26 km and 900 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Tržič to Podljubelj
sections.body: Start opposite the bus station and ride north through the old town toward Podljubelj. Village streets give way to the valley approach; parking and services are still close if you need a last stop.
sections.body2: Beyond the village, a gravel link runs beside the main road toward Ljubelj before you briefly join the tunnel approach. Traffic here is real, ride assertively and predictably.

sections.title: The old pass
sections.body: Before the tunnel, peel right onto the historic road. Thirteen hairpins and raw gradient remain. This is the section shared with hikers and, one September Sunday, vintage race cars, the rest of the year it belongs to legs and lungs.
sections.body2: The pass hut is the turnaround. Eat, look into Austria, then descend the same way with cool brakes and eyes up for oncoming riders.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Budget about three hours and 26 km out-and-back. Pin the hut opening and a recovery café in Tržič before you start the steep finale.
sections.body2: Open K35 in Zyflow for navigation on the mixed surfaces, and keep a weather eye on the saddle, it turns quickly at 1,370 m.

k42-roznovenska.lede: Tržič’s culture-forward loop through Brezje pri Tržiču, pilgrimage landmarks, valley towns and touring pace without a high pass.
k42-roznovenska.intro: K42 is for mixed groups and heritage days: quieter roads, churches and villages, and enough distance to feel complete without Košuta’s commitment.
k42-roznovenska.metaDescription: Cultural ride from Tržič through Brezje pri Tržiču: 369 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Valley heritage
sections.body: Link Tržič with Brezje pri Tržiču. Café density is kinder than on the alpine set; photo stops come naturally.
sections.body2: Gradients stay friendly. This is the day you bring someone who loves places more than watts.

sections.title: Pace and pauses
sections.body: Do not rush the squares and churches, they are the point. Ride assertively on busier connectors, then slow again in village cores.
sections.body2: A bakery stop on the return seals the tone of the route.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Save lunch pins along the corridor and treat K42 as a warm-up before harder Tržič days.
sections.body2: Open the route in Zyflow to keep cultural stops and navigation on one map.

k43-dobrca.lede: A serious alpine day from Tržič toward Dobrča, long climbs, ridge air and the feeling of riding the Karawanks rather than around them.
k43-dobrca.intro: K43 sits with the harder Tržič alpine set: sustained climbing, thinner traffic higher up, and panoramas that justify an early start.
k43-dobrca.metaDescription: Ride from Tržič up to the hut on Dobrča: 2067 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Toward the ridge
sections.body: Climb out of town into forest roads that refuse to flatten. Patience matters more than peak power.
sections.body2: Pack layers. Exposure increases as trees thin and the ridge wind finds you.

sections.title: Dobrča rewards
sections.body: Wide Karawanks views are the payment for the morning’s work. Turn around with time for a careful descent.
sections.body2: This is not a café-hopping loop, carry food and respect weather windows.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Mark emergency descents and a recovery stop in Tržič. Check conditions before the final push.
sections.body2: Open K43 in Zyflow so the line and bail-outs stay visible when fog or fatigue set in.

k51-udin-borst.lede: Foothill gravel around Udin boršt, forest tracks, gentle rollers and adventure without a high pass.
k51-udin-borst.intro: K51 is the confident gravel day of the Tržič shortlist: more dirt than asphalt, still close enough to town that a café finish is easy.
k51-udin-borst.metaDescription: Gravel loop through the Udin boršt forest from Tržič: 286 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Forest edge riding
sections.body: Mix valley approaches with tracks through the boršt. Expect roots, soft patches after rain and the pleasure of canopy shade.
sections.body2: Keep tyre pressure honest. Slick clay turns playful into careful.

sections.title: Turn back when you like
sections.body: The beauty of this loop family is flexibility, extend into the reserve or shorten toward asphalt whenever energy dips.
sections.body2: Shared paths mean modest speeds near walkers.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin a café return in Tržič and an exit to asphalt if the forest turns muddy.
sections.body2: Open K51 in Zyflow to see the gravel corridor beside the easier K52 bells loop.

k52-pot-treh-zvonov.lede: The easy family loop of the Tržič set, gentle terrain, village bells and a rhythm that works for mixed abilities.
k52-pot-treh-zvonov.intro: K52 is the gateway ride: approachable distance and gradient, still unmistakably Gorenjska countryside around Tržič. Bring kids, recovery legs or anyone new to the local roads.
k52-pot-treh-zvonov.metaDescription: Easy family loop on the Path of Three Bells near Tržič: 144 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Bells and villages
sections.body: Quiet roads and short connectors pass churches and hamlets. The “three bells” idea is the cultural thread, stop, listen, keep rolling.
sections.body2: Surfaces stay friendly. This is gravel-lite at most, not a mud-fest.

sections.title: A first local day
sections.body: Use K52 to learn the basin before you attempt Ljubelj. Landmarks stick; confidence builds.
sections.body2: Ice cream and water stops are part of the design, do not optimise them away.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Save family-friendly pins before you roll out. Keep the map zoomed for short decisions.
sections.body2: Open K52 in Zyflow as the soft entry to the Tržič catalogue.

k53-kriva-jelka.lede: Into the Udin boršt nature reserve toward the crooked fir, shaded tracks and a landmark finish in the forest.
k53-kriva-jelka.intro: K53 targets one of the area’s best-known forest landmarks. Expect soft ground after rain and a calmer alternative to the high alpine days above Tržič.
k53-kriva-jelka.metaDescription: Gravel ride to Kriva jelka in Udin boršt: 386 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Reserve tracks
sections.body: Enter Udin boršt and follow forest roads toward Kriva jelka. The canopy keeps the day cool; the landmark gives the ride a story.
sections.body2: Share space with walkers. Announce yourself and keep speeds modest near the tree.

sections.title: Nature-first riding
sections.body: This is not about elevation bragging rights. It is about quiet kilometres and a destination that locals name with a smile.
sections.body2: If trails are saturated, divert to firmer connectors, the reserve prefers restraint.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin an asphalt exit and a town café. Pair with K51 or K52 for a gravel weekend without alpine weather risk.
sections.body2: Open K53 in Zyflow to keep the reserve line obvious among similar forest tracks.

k55-gozd-udin-borst.lede: A varied foothill loop linking Gozd with Udin boršt, more climbing than the family routes, still short of alpine grades.
k55-gozd-udin-borst.intro: K55 sits between easy bells and hard passes: useful when you want sweat without committing to Ljubelj or Košuta.
k55-gozd-udin-borst.metaDescription: Foothill gravel between Gozd and Udin boršt: 763 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Gozd to the boršt
sections.body: Link the Gozd side with Udin boršt tracks. Expect mixed surfaces and short punches rather than one long climb.
sections.body2: Navigation matters, similar junctions repeat. A saved line prevents accidental extras.

sections.title: Training without drama
sections.body: Use this as a midweek spin or a bridge day between culture and alpine plans. Elevation adds up without exposure.
sections.body2: After rain, choose the firmer options; clay sections get ugly fast.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin a bakery return to Tržič and keep K55 beside K51/K52 on your map for mix-and-match weekends.
sections.body2: Open the route in Zyflow so the foothill corridor stays clear.

kamnicanka.lede: The gentlest petal of the Kranjska roža: seventy kilometres of valley touring past castles, churches and Arboretum Volčji Potok, with barely 250 m of climbing.
kamnicanka.intro: Kamničanka is the route you give someone on their first day in Gorenjska. It leaves Kranj on quiet roads, crosses Slovenia’s only motorway bike bridge near Vokle, and threads heritage stops all the way to Kamnik before a soft return through forest gravel and the Sava plain. Distance without drama, and still a full day that feels like a real tour.
kamnicanka.metaDescription: Kamničanka from Kranj past Kamnik and Arboretum Volčji Potok: 70 km and 254 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: From Kranj across the plain
sections.body: Roll out through Šenčur toward Adergas, where the Church of the Annunciation sits in open fields. The Češnjevek ponds and Strmol Castle follow soon after, then Grad near Cerklje, a string of stops that never forces a hard climb.
sections.body2: Komenda’s oak woodland brings you to the edge of Kamnik. The old town is the natural lunch stop: short alleys, cafés, and enough shade to reset before the arboretum leg.

sections.title: Arboretum, gravel and home
sections.body: From Šmarca the path reaches Arboretum Volčji Potok. Give it time, the park is one of the best mid-ride pauses in the flower network. Then Radomlje and Mengeš lead toward Vodice.
sections.body2: The stretch from Vodice toward Voglje turns to good gravel under forest canopy. Back into Kranj the road flattens again: tidy asphalt, easy spinning, and a finish that still has battery to spare on an e-bike.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Mark a charger and a long lunch in Kamnik before you leave. If you want coffee with a view of bikes parked properly, filter for bike-friendly places along the loop.
sections.body2: At 70 km and only 254 m of climbing this is the safest warm-up before Blejčanka or the Tržič alpine days. Save the GPX, then open the same line in Zyflow when you are ready to navigate.

ljubljancanka.lede: South from Kranj to the capital: countryside connectors, Smlednik Castle, then Tivoli and Ljubljana Castle as the urban climax of the day.
ljubljancanka.intro: Ljubljančanka is the city petal of the flower network, enough rural kilometres to feel like a tour, then a clear arrival in Ljubljana. At about 70 km it suits riders who want heritage and café density without alpine grades.
ljubljancanka.metaDescription: Ljubljančanka, Kranj to Ljubljana past Smlednik Castle: 70 km and 460 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Countryside approach
sections.body: Leave Kranj on valley roads that gradually trade Gorenjska fields for the Ljubljana basin. Smlednik Castle is the landmark on the approach, a good photo and stretch stop.
sections.body2: Keep an eye on busier connectors as you near the city. The ride is not technical; the challenge is attention in mixed traffic.

sections.title: Into Ljubljana
sections.body: Tivoli offers a green entry, then the climb or walk up to Ljubljana Castle for the classic finish frame. Old-town streets below are dense with bike-friendly cafés if you filter for them.
sections.body2: Return north the way you came, or rail-assist one direction if you prefer a one-way day. Either way, save battery for the urban segment.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin a lunch spot near the castle hill and a charger before the return. City traffic rewards a calm pace and clear routing.
sections.body2: Open Ljubljančanka in Zyflow to keep navigation and place layers together, especially useful when streets get busy around the centre.

locanka.lede: Kranj to Škofja Loka: stone bridges, castle hill and Crngrob on one of the flower’s prettiest heritage days.
locanka.intro: Ločanka is the heritage favourite of the Kranjska roža, slightly shorter than Blejčanka, denser in old-town atmosphere. You ride into a medieval basin that still feels painted, with Capuchin bridges and a castle above the confluence.
locanka.metaTitle: Ločanka (64 km to Škofja Loka) | Zyflow
locanka.metaDescription: Ločanka, Kranj to Škofja Loka's old town and castle: 64 km and 930 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Toward the Loka basin
sections.body: Leave Kranj on rolling connectors that tip you into the Škofja Loka landscape. The castle hill appears before the streets do, a useful landmark for pacing the day.
sections.body2: Traffic is manageable if you keep to the signed cycling links. Save energy for wandering once you reach the centre.

sections.title: Old town and Crngrob
sections.body: Škofja Loka’s twin bridges and lanes are the main event. Walk sections if crowds are thick; the point is the place, not average speed.
sections.body2: A short detour to Crngrob adds the frescoed church many riders miss. Then turn for Kranj with a café stop still in the bag.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Pin a long lunch in the old town and a quieter return road. At around 64 km this fits neatly between a recovery spin and a full mountain day.
sections.body2: Open Ločanka in Zyflow to navigate the approach and keep bike-friendly cafés visible when you arrive.

mali-vrh.lede: A calm Jezersko half-day on forest road to the Mali vrh lookout, Virnikov Grintovec, Košuta and Storžič in one panoramic out-and-back.
mali-vrh.intro: Mali vrh is the gentle panorama of the Jezersko set. From the TIC in Zgornje Jezersko you cross a wooden bridge toward Makekova Kočna, climb kindly on forest road, pause at the built lookout, then continue to a bench at the end of the road above the Kokra.
mali-vrh.metaDescription: Jezersko lookout under Mali vrh, out and back from Zgornje Jezersko: 17.3 km and 596 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Toward Makekova Kočna
sections.body: Orient at the panoramic board near the TIC, then take the asphalt toward Makekova Kočna until the fork for the farm. Stay straight onto the forest road that rises without drama.
sections.body2: After roughly four kilometres the arranged lookout under Mali vrh appears on a sharp left bend, the first big view toward Virnikov Grintovec, Komatevra, Stegovnik, Storžič and the Košuta ridge.

sections.title: End bench and return
sections.body: Continue on the same easy forest grade to the end of the road. The bench overlooks the Kokra and Jezerska Kočna, a quiet turnaround.
sections.body2: Retrace the same line. Share space with hikers and keep speeds down on the shaded descent.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: About 17.3 km and 596 m with roughly three hours on the clock. Pin the TIC and a valley café for afterwards.
sections.body2: Open Mali vrh in Zyflow when you want this short alpine spin beside Ravenska Kočna or Jezerski vrh for a multi-day Jezersko stay.

ravenska-kocna.lede: Past Planšarsko jezero into Ravenska Kočna and up to Štularjeva planina, cirque walls, a cargo cableway and one of Jezersko’s most photogenic half-days.
ravenska-kocna.intro: Ravenska Kočna is the postcard alpine loop of the valley: lake at the mouth, glacial walls ahead, and a final climb to Štularjeva planina facing Skuta. About 16.6 km and 408 m keep it ambitious but approachable.
ravenska-kocna.metaDescription: Ravenska Kočna past Planšarsko jezero to Štularjeva planina: 16.6 km and 408 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Lake into the valley
sections.body: From the TIC ride to Planšarsko jezero and skirt it on the right. At the Pod Turni hunting lodge the barrier allows cyclists through into Ravenska Kočna.
sections.body2: Asphalt becomes gravel past Ancel farm. Follow past the thematic path rest area and the car park to the lower station of the cargo cableway for Češka koča.

sections.title: Štularjeva planina
sections.body: Turn right for the last two kilometres of climbing. On the pasture, take time for the cirque toward Skuta and the surrounding peaks to Goli vrh.
sections.body2: Descend the same way with hikers in mind. Pause again at the lake, it earns a slow finish in every season.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Roughly 2 hours 15 minutes if you ride steadily. Pin the lake café options and respect shared trail etiquette.
sections.body2: Open Ravenska Kočna in Zyflow beside Mali vrh for a two-loop Jezersko day with a swim or coffee between.

spodnji-virnik.lede: The shortest Jezersko ride: the tufa quarry, an active rock-forming spring and Spodnji Virnik farm with dairy worth packing out.
spodnji-virnik.intro: Spodnji Virnik is the curiosity loop, geology you can watch happening, one steep pitch you may walk, and an organic farm finish with Grintovci views. About 9.4 km and 304 m in roughly ninety minutes.
spodnji-virnik.metaDescription: Short Jezersko loop to the tufa quarry and Spodnji Virnik farm: 9.4 km and 304 m of climbing. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: Into the Kokra side valley
sections.body: Drop from Zgornje Jezersko to Spodnji Kraj and turn toward the upper Kokra. Virnikov Grintovec appears on the right as you roll the valley floor.
sections.body2: Past the first rise you reach tufa stacks and the active spring where calcium carbonate is still depositing rock. It is the educational heart of the ride.

sections.title: Farm and spring walk
sections.body: After the stream crossing a short steep climb leads toward Spodnji Virnik. Leave the bike and walk minutes to the spring; then taste cheeses, yogurt and skuta at the farm if they are offering.
sections.body2: Descend the gravel to the main road and spin home. One punchy pitch is walkable, still an easy win among short rides.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Bring a backpack for dairy. Pin the farm and the TIC so the short loop never feels lost.
sections.body2: Open Spodnji Virnik in Zyflow as the rest-day or evening spin beside the bigger Jezersko panoramas.

trzicanka.lede: Kranj’s northern petal into Tržič, old-town streets, Kamen Castle ruins and the gateway to Ljubelj, Košuta and Udin boršt.
trzicanka.intro: Tržičanka connects the Kranj flower to the Tržič alpine catalogue. Ride it as a destination day into a historic basin under the Karawanks, or as the approach before a harder pass the next morning.
trzicanka.metaDescription: Tržičanka, Kranj to Tržič through the Kokra canyon and on to Kamen Castle: 68 km. Open in Zyflow.

sections.title: North into the basin
sections.body: Valley riding from Kranj builds toward Tržič’s gateway feel. The landscape tightens; the town’s historic core and factory heritage sit under steep forest walls.
sections.body2: Kamen Castle’s ruins are the classic spur stop, a short climb for a wide view back over the valley.

sections.title: Tržič as a hub
sections.body: Once in town you stand at the start of K35 Ljubelj, the Košuta pastures and the softer Udin boršt gravel days. Use Tržičanka to arrive fresh enough to explore the centre.
sections.body2: Cafés and supplies are denser here than on the high routes. Stock up before you commit to anything steeper.

sections.title: How to ride it with Zyflow
sections.body: Save Tržičanka as a transfer day, then chain K35 or K52 from the same map. Pin a charger in town if you are on an e-bike.
sections.body2: Open the route in Zyflow for the approach navigation, then browse nearby alpine lines without leaving the app.
